records.source: **WHAT IT IS FOR.** Every screen that shows objects has had its own way of finding them, and the Embeddings screen had none at all -- :meth:`spacr.qt.screens.embeddings.EmbeddingsScreen.set_crops` existed and nothing in ``spacr/`` called it, so the only route to a label-free vector was to open Python. records.context: **What it is for.** Every application view that shows objects has had its own way of finding them, and the Embeddings application view had none at all -- :meth:`spacr.qt.screens.embeddings.EmbeddingsScreen.set_crops` existed and nothing in ``spacr/`` called it, so the only route to a label-free vector was to open Python. This module is the missing half: it turns a question about a plate into a stack of pixels, and it does it in two steps so a GUI can stay answerable between them.
records.translation: **PARA QUÉ SIRVE.** Cada pantalla que muestra objetos ha tenido su propia forma de encontrarlos, y la pantalla Embeddings no tenía ninguna -- :meth:`spacr.qt.screens.embeddings.EmbeddingsScreen.set_crops` existía y nada en ``spacr/`` la llamaba, así que la única vía hacia un vector sin etiquetas era abrir Python. Este módulo es la mitad que faltaba: convierte una pregunta sobre una placa en una pila de píxeles, y lo hace en dos pasos para que una GUI pueda seguir respondiendo entre ellos.
records.review_basis: MT draft edited in AI review

records.label: spacr.crop_loader#2
records.source: **PLANNING IS NOT LOADING, and that separation is the whole design.** :func:`plan_crops` asks the database or the folder *which objects match* and reads no pixels at all: a ``COUNT`` and a ``SELECT`` of identifiers, or one ``scandir``. It is milliseconds on a plate of sixty thousand crops, so a screen can run it on a click and tell the user what they asked for before committing to reading any of it. :func:`load_crops` then reads the pixels in pages, reporting after each one. A caller that runs the second half on a worker thread gets a progress number per page and a stop that takes effect within a page rather than at the end.
records.context: **Planning is not loading, and that separation is the whole design.** :func:`plan_crops` asks the database or the folder *which objects match* and reads no pixels at all: a ``COUNT`` and a ``SELECT`` of identifiers, or one ``scandir``. It is milliseconds on a plate of sixty thousand extracted image regions, so a screen can execute it on a click and tell the user what they asked for before committing to reading any of it. :func:`load_crops` then reads the pixels in pages, reporting after each one. A caller that executes the second half on a background execution unit gets a progress number per page and a stop that takes effect within a page rather than at the end.
records.translation: **PLANIFICAR NO ES CARGAR, y esa separación es todo el diseño.** :func:`plan_crops` pregunta a la base de datos o a la carpeta *qué objetos coinciden* y no lee ningún píxel: un ``COUNT`` y un ``SELECT`` de identificadores, o un único ``scandir``. Tarda milisegundos en una placa de sesenta mil recortes, así que una pantalla puede ejecutarlo con un clic y decir al usuario lo que ha pedido antes de comprometerse a leer nada. Después, :func:`load_crops` lee los píxeles por páginas e informa tras cada una. Quien ejecute la segunda mitad en un hilo de trabajo obtiene un número de progreso por página y una detención que surte efecto dentro de una página en lugar de al final.

records.context: **A cap is part of the answer, not a failure to load everything.** Sixty thousand extracted image regions of 96x96x3 is 1.6 GB before a backbone has seen one of them, and a screen that tries it dies on a machine that could have embedded the first two thousand happily. So :attr:`CropQuery.limit` is a real default and the plan says what it left behind -- "the first 2,000 of 61,433" -- rather than quietly returning a subset that looks like the whole plate.
records.translation: **UN TOPE FORMA PARTE DE LA RESPUESTA, NO UN FALLO AL CARGAR LA TOTALIDAD.** Sesenta mil recortes de 96x96x3 son 1.6 GB antes de que una red troncal haya visto uno solo, y una pantalla que lo intenta se bloquea en una máquina que habría incrustado sin problemas los dos mil primeros. Por eso :attr:`CropQuery.limit` es un valor predeterminado real y el plan dice lo que dejó fuera -- "los primeros 2,000 de 61,433" -- en lugar de devolver en silencio un subconjunto que parece la placa entera.

records.source: **AND A CAP IS NOT THE ONLY THING THAT REMOVES A ROW, SO IT IS COUNTED ON ITS OWN.** The merged route drops every row it cannot cut, and reporting that as a cap is the same sentence read backwards: a complete answer dressed as a subset, telling the user to raise a limit that never bit. So :attr:`CropPlan.matched`, :attr:`CropPlan.selected` and :attr:`CropPlan.count` are three numbers, :attr:`CropPlan.capped` is the gap between the first two and :attr:`CropPlan.dropped` the gap between the last two, and they reach the panel as separate clauses.

So :attr:`CropPlan.matched`, :attr:`CropPlan.selected` and :attr:`CropPlan.count` are three numbers, :attr:`CropPlan.capped` is the gap between the first two and :attr:`CropPlan.dropped` the gap between the last two, and they reach the panel as separate clauses.
records.translation: **Y UN TOPE NO ES LO ÚNICO QUE ELIMINA UNA FILA, ASÍ QUE SE CUENTA POR SEPARADO.** La ruta fusionada descarta cada fila que no puede cortar, y notificarlo como un tope es la misma frase leída al revés: una respuesta completa disfrazada de subconjunto, que le dice al usuario que aumente un límite que nunca llegó a actuar. Por eso :attr:`CropPlan.matched`, :attr:`CropPlan.selected` y :attr:`CropPlan.count` son tres números, :attr:`CropPlan.capped` es la diferencia entre los dos primeros y :attr:`CropPlan.dropped` la diferencia entre los dos últimos, y llegan al panel como cláusulas separadas.

records.label: spacr.diameter#6
records.source: 1. **Flatten.** Denoise with a 1 px Gaussian, then subtract a heavily smoothed copy (sigma = max(32, min(H, W) / 4)) to remove illumination gradients. The sigma is deliberately far larger than any plausible object so that flattening removes vignetting without eating the objects — the opposite trade-off (a tight rolling ball) shrinks what it is trying to measure. 2. **Reject noise.** Compare the structural amplitude of the flattened plane (p99 - p30) against the *pixel-level* noise scale, measured as ``1.4826 * MAD(img - gaussian(img, 1))`` on the raw plane. A pure-noise plane scores below 1; a plane with real objects scores in the tens. Below ``min_snr`` the field is discarded rather than thresholded, because Otsu will happily bisect pure noise and hand back a confident-looking number. 3. **Threshold and label.** Otsu, fill holes, label, drop components that touch the image border (truncated, so their size is a lie) and components that are absurd (equivalent diameter below ``min_object_diameter``, or area above ``max_object_fraction`` of the field). Sizes are equivalent diameters, ``2 * sqrt(area / pi)``. 4. **Drop specks, then take the median.** A textured or punctate stain (a mitochondrial cell stain, a parasite marker) thresholds into a few whole objects plus hundreds of 4-10 px specks, and a plain median counts every speck as an object: on spaCR's own test plate that put the cell at 8 px and the pathogen at 11 px against 175 px and 32 px in the curated masks, while the nucleus, whose stain is solid, came out right at 91 px. So the typical object is first located by the stained area it carries (the area-weighted median, which specks cannot move because they hold almost no area), everything narrower than :data:`SPECK_FRACTION` of it is dropped, and the characteristic size is the median of what remains. Small components that together hold :data:`SPECK_MAX_AREA_SHARE` of the stained area or more are a second population, not specks, and stay. 5. **Cross-check by distance transform.** Step 3 has one dominant failure mode: a confluent monolayer fuses into a single component, that component touches the border and is dropped, and the estimate is then computed from whatever debris survived — biased **low**, and silently. So the Euclidean distance transform of the (unfilled) foreground is computed as well, its local maxima are taken as one seed per object (two passes: a coarse pass sets the suppression radius for the refined pass), and a watershed on ``-EDT`` splits the fused foreground back into objects whose equivalent diameters are measured the same way.
records.context: 1. **Flatten.** Denoise with a 1 px Gaussian, then subtract a heavily smoothed copy (sigma = max(32, min(H, W) / 4)) to remove illumination gradients. The sigma is deliberately far larger than any plausible object so that flattening removes vignetting without eating the objects — the opposite trade-off (a tight rolling ball) shrinks what it is trying to measure. 2. **Reject noise.** Compare the structural amplitude of the flattened plane (p99 - p30) against the *pixel-level* noise scale, measured as ``1.4826 * MAD(img - gaussian(img, 1))`` on the raw plane. A pure-noise plane scores below 1; a plane with real objects scores in the tens. Below ``min_snr`` the field is discarded rather than thresholded, because Otsu will happily bisect pure noise and hand back a confident-looking number. 3. **Threshold and label.** Otsu, fill holes, label, drop components that touch the image border (truncated, so their size is a lie) and components that are absurd (equivalent diameter below ``min_object_diameter``, or area above ``max_object_fraction`` of the field). Small components that together hold :data:`SPECK_MAX_AREA_SHARE` of the stained area or more are a second population, not specks, and stay. 5. **Cross-check by distance transform.** Step 3 has one dominant failure mode: a confluent monolayer fuses into a single component, that component touches the border and is dropped, and the estimate is then computed from whatever debris survived — biased **low**, and silently. So the Euclidean distance transform of the (unfilled) foreground is computed as well, its local maxima are taken as one seed per object (two passes: a coarse pass sets the suppression radius for the refined pass), and a watershed on ``-EDT`` splits the fused foreground back into objects whose equivalent diameters are measured the same way.
records.translation: 1. **Aplanar.** Se elimina el ruido con un filtro gaussiano de 1 px y luego se resta una copia muy suavizada (sigma = max(32, min(H, W) / 4)) para eliminar los gradientes de iluminación. La sigma es deliberadamente mucho mayor que cualquier objeto plausible, para que el aplanado elimine el viñeteado sin comerse los objetos — el compromiso contrario (una bola rodante ajustada) encoge lo que intenta medir. 2. **Rechazar el ruido.** Se compara la amplitud estructural del plano aplanado (p99 - p30) con la escala de ruido *a nivel de píxel*, medida como ``1.4826 * MAD(img - gaussian(img, 1))`` sobre el plano sin procesar. Un plano de ruido puro puntúa por debajo de 1; un plano con objetos reales puntúa en las decenas. Por debajo de ``min_snr``, el campo se descarta en lugar de umbralizarse, porque Otsu dividirá alegremente en dos el ruido puro y devolverá un número de aspecto fiable. 3. **Umbralizar y etiquetar.** Otsu, relleno de huecos, etiquetado, y se descartan los componentes que tocan el borde de la imagen (truncados, así que su tamaño es engañoso) y los componentes absurdos (diámetro equivalente inferior a ``min_object_diameter``, o área superior a ``max_object_fraction`` del campo). Los tamaños son diámetros equivalentes, ``2 * sqrt(area / pi)``. 4. **Descartar las motas y luego tomar la mediana.** Una tinción texturizada o puntiforme (una tinción mitocondrial de células, un marcador de parásitos) se umbraliza en unos pocos objetos completos más cientos de motas de 4-10 px, y una mediana simple cuenta cada mota como un objeto: en la propia placa de prueba de spaCR, eso situaba la célula en 8 px y el patógeno en 11 px frente a 175 px y 32 px en las máscaras curadas, mientras que el núcleo, cuya tinción es sólida, salía correcto en 91 px. Por eso, primero se localiza el objeto típico por el área teñida que contiene (la mediana ponderada por área, que las motas no pueden desplazar porque apenas tienen área), se descarta todo lo más estrecho que :data:`SPECK_FRACTION` de él, y el tamaño característico es la mediana de lo que queda. Los componentes pequeños que en conjunto contienen :data:`SPECK_MAX_AREA_SHARE` o más del área teñida son una segunda población, no motas, y se conservan. 5. **Comprobación cruzada mediante la transformada de distancia.** El paso 3 tiene un modo de fallo dominante: una monocapa confluente se fusiona en un único componente, ese componente toca el borde y se descarta, y la estimación se calcula entonces a partir de los restos que hayan sobrevivido — sesgada a la **baja**, y en silencio. Por eso también se calcula la transformada de distancia euclidiana del primer plano (sin rellenar), sus máximos locales se toman como una semilla por objeto (dos pasadas: una pasada gruesa fija el radio de supresión para la pasada refinada), y una segmentación watershed sobre ``-EDT`` vuelve a dividir el primer plano fusionado en objetos cuyos diámetros equivalentes se miden de la misma manera.
